metadata.title: Ask Whether, Never What: Checking a Pipeline's Keys Without Reading Them
metadata.voice: Kokoro am_onyx, speed 1.0, each beat synthesised whole
metadata.timing: measured from the rendered beat audio (mp3/timings.json); Whisper small.en word clock stored there

beats.title: INTRODUCTION
beats.narration_text: Hi, this is Tanmay Kulkarni, for Humanitarians AI. This week I contributed to Mycroft, a public repository where work is written as recipes that an agent can run and a person can read.
beats.visual_intent: Title card from the first frame: the film's title, and the repo name. Empty row outline beside it, six small step markers, none lit.

beats.title: SIX STEPS, NOTHING TOUCHED
beats.narration_text: One command. Six steps run in order, and the last line says: all six steps completed. In all that time, nothing was contacted, and no key's value was kept. How does a pipeline get ready to run without touching anything it needs?
beats.visual_intent: Terminal: `node scripts/snickerdoodle.mjs run scenariostresstestingagent --sample`; six markers light in turn; last line `All 6 steps completed.` (a fresh recording, not the scratch-copy transcript; `sample mode` visible on screen). Then the empty row outline returns, labelled `?`.

beats.title: WHAT THIS IS
beats.narration_text: The recipe is a stress test: hand it an invented set of holdings and a market fall, and it adds up the damage. I have built five of its six steps in earlier weeks. This week is step two, which comes right after the provenance check: before any request is checked or any tool runs, it lists what the pipeline would reach for.
beats.visual_intent: Recipe `scenariostresstestingagent.md`, step list with step two highlighted; `todos_open: 0`. Label: `Source and Credential Check`.

beats.title: THREE FACTS, NOT ONE
beats.narration_text: A pipeline that reaches outside depends on things: a service to call, a key to call it with. About each one there are three different facts. Is it there? Who has to say yes? And what is the value? They feel like one question. They are three.
beats.visual_intent: Three empty cells appear one at a time: `is it there`, `who says yes`, `the value`. The third is drawn with a closed lid.

beats.title: ONE ROW
beats.narration_text: The workflow names four sources. Let me follow one: the model call. It gets a row. A name, the Groq chat model, an AI model hosted by a company. A status: approval required. And a reason, in plain words: a live model call, and sample mode, the practice mode with invented data, never makes one.
beats.visual_intent: `source-check.json`, the Groq source: `node`, `status`, `reason` fill into the row cell by cell. Other three sources dim at the edge.

beats.title: IS IT THERE
beats.narration_text: Now the first fact. The row carries the key's name, on screen now, and the script asks the program's settings, the environment, one question: is a variable with this name set? The answer is a yes or a no. Here it is no. The value is never stored, and never written to a file.
beats.visual_intent: Cell `credential_env: GROQ_API_KEY`; cell `credential_present: false` fills. The lid on the value cell stays shut. Script excerpt: `bool(os.environ.get(env_name))` highlighted.

beats.title: WHY A YES OR A NO
beats.narration_text: Why so careful? A value can end up in a log, a report, a screenshot, a message. A yes or a no cannot. Whatever the page says, there is nothing in it to copy.
beats.visual_intent: The value cell with its lid; four small icons (log, report, screenshot, message) each receive `no` and nothing else.

beats.title: WHO SAYS YES
beats.narration_text: The second fact. Approval record: none. Approved for live action: false. Live call performed: false. The page does not decide anything. It records that a person has not yet said yes, because saying yes is a person's act.
beats.visual_intent: Cells `approval_record_present: false`, `approved_for_live_action: false`, `live_call_performed: false` fill. Top of file: `live_calls: false`, `network: false`.

beats.title: THE OTHER THREE
beats.narration_text: Beside it, the other sources. The webhook is available: twenty-two invented requests, each with a fingerprint recorded when the set was fixed, checked before each one is kept as it was. Twelve are clean, ten are faulty, none rejected. Chat is skipped, with a reason. The other live service is approval required, like the first. Every source lands in one of those states, with a reason.
beats.visual_intent: Four rows together. For the webhook: `records: 22`, audit table `clean 12 / defective 10 / rejected 0`. Hand-off line: `every source is available, skipped with a reason, or approval-required: met`.

beats.title: THE PUZZLE
beats.narration_text: Then a small puzzle. To prove the script never leaks a key, the test needs a key. A made-up key typed into a test file can look, to a reader or a scanner, like a real one that leaked. So the test builds two dummy values while it runs, from pieces, and they exist only until it ends.
beats.visual_intent: Left: the test's source with the dummy built from joined pieces (`"-".join([...])`), the comment `assembled at run time so no credential-shaped text sits in this file`. Nothing key-shaped anywhere on screen.

beats.title: THE HARD CASE
beats.narration_text: Now the hard case: set both keys. The page says yes, twice, and the values appear in no file the step writes and not on the screen. And every question the script puts to the environment is a yes or a no. Thirty-seven checks pass, this among them. To test a promise to keep a secret, I first had to make one that was safe to lose.
beats.visual_intent: Split, held at least two seconds together: left, the two rows with `credential_present: true`; right, the scan of the written files and the screen finding nothing (`found: none`). Counter `37 of 37`. Closing line on screen: `a secret that is safe to lose`.

beats.title: WHAT YOU GET
beats.narration_text: And what you get is simple. Clone the repository, run the command, and read one page that says what a live run would need, with nothing contacted.
beats.visual_intent: `ingest-audit.md` rendered: the table of nodes, status, credential name, `Set in the environment`; footer line `A credential is reported only as set or not set; its value is never read.`

beats.title: YOUR TURN
beats.narration_text: So here is a small exercise. Take one thing your own pipeline reaches for. Write three lines: is it there, who has to say yes, what is the value. Fill in the first two. Then design the third so that nothing downstream ever needs it.
beats.visual_intent: Three blank lines on a card, the first two filling with an example (`SERVICE_KEY` / `set: no` / `approval: none`), the third left closed.

beats.title: CLOSE
beats.narration_text: The recipe stays a draft by design. Going live is the next piece, and that is a person's call. Step two arrived in pull request eighty five, and it is merged.

beats.title: SIGN-OFF
beats.narration_text: Tanmay Kulkarni, for Humanitarians AI, signing off.
